disclaimer: Illustrative planning scenarios, not forecasts of job loss.

gradual.label: Scenario A: Gradual AI Transformation
assumptions: Generative AI tools are adopted step by step over roughly 5-10 years, mostly augmenting existing tasks.
Employers keep most existing roles and redesign the tasks inside them.
Training and reskilling programmes keep pace with tool adoption.
Regulation and data governance mature alongside adoption.

rapid.label: Scenario B: Rapid AI Transformation
assumptions: AI capability and enterprise adoption accelerate sharply within roughly 2-4 years.
Routine analytical, coding and content tasks are increasingly automated inside roles.
Entry-level task mixes change faster than training pipelines can adjust.
Demand shifts toward judgement, oversight, domain knowledge and AI-orchestration skills.

gradual: Add AI-assisted analysis to your workflow while keeping SQL and spreadsheet fundamentals sharp.
Build 2-3 dashboards, each with a short written insight narrative.
Learn basic statistics so you can sanity-check automated outputs.
rapid: Shift effort from manual report production to problem framing, validation and storytelling.
Practise reviewing and testing AI-generated queries and charts.
Build domain depth (for example finance, health or logistics) that tools cannot supply on their own.

gradual: Keep core modelling and statistics strong while learning to use LLM tooling for prototyping.
Publish a project that explains modelling choices and limitations in plain language.
Learn model evaluation and bias checks.
rapid: Move toward experiment design, evaluation and model oversight, which are harder to automate.
Learn to build with and evaluate foundation models, not only train models from scratch.
Develop responsible-AI and data-governance fluency.

gradual: Adopt AI coding assistants while still writing and understanding the code yourself.
Strengthen testing and code-review habits.
Pick up secure-coding basics.
rapid: Invest in system design, requirements clarification and reviewing AI-generated code for correctness and security.
Build the habit of writing tests and specifications first.
Practise explaining technical trade-offs to non-technical people.

gradual: Build one end-to-end ML project and deploy it behind an API.
Learn the basics of working with LLM APIs and retrieval.
Document data sources and limitations.
rapid: Prioritise deployment, monitoring and evaluation of AI systems over model training alone.
Learn cloud and MLOps tooling.
Build responsible-AI practices into every project.

gradual: Use AI tools to draft requirements and process maps, then refine them with stakeholders.
Learn enough SQL to check numbers yourself.
Practise facilitation and workshop skills.
rapid: Focus on stakeholder trust, negotiation and judging which problems are worth solving.
Learn to validate AI-generated analysis against real business context.
Build domain expertise in one sector.

gradual: Use generative tools for exploration and keep hands-on prototyping skills.
Do real user interviews and write up findings.
Learn accessibility standards.
rapid: Lean into research, strategy and design judgement, since layout production is increasingly automated.
Learn to direct and critique AI-generated designs.
Build skills in measuring design impact with data.

gradual: Use AI for drafts and variations while keeping a distinct brand voice.
Learn to read campaign analytics with confidence.
Run a small real campaign and document the results.
rapid: Move from producing content to strategy, brand judgement and experimentation.
Learn to measure and attribute campaign performance.
Build trust and transparency practices around AI-generated content.

gradual: Practise on hands-on labs and capture-the-flag exercises.
Learn scripting to automate repetitive monitoring tasks.
Study one major cloud platform's security model.
rapid: Learn to defend against AI-assisted attacks and to supervise AI-assisted detection tools.
Strengthen risk communication for non-technical leaders.
Build automation skills in Python.

gradual: Use AI assistants for status reports and planning drafts.
Earn a recognised project-management foundation.
Practise leading a real team project.
rapid: Invest in leadership, change management and risk judgement as admin tasks get automated.
Learn to use data to track delivery.
Learn how AI changes team workflows and roles.

gradual: Earn a cloud fundamentals certificate and build a small deployed project.
Learn infrastructure-as-code.
Add security basics.
rapid: Focus on architecture, security and cost governance, with automation handling routine setup.
Learn to review AI-generated infrastructure code.
Pick up Python for automation.

gradual: Pilot AI tools in a lesson or training module and gather learner feedback.
Learn learning-analytics basics.
Stay current with education-technology policy.
rapid: Specialise in pedagogy, assessment integrity and AI-literacy teaching, which tools do not replace.
Learn to evaluate AI learning tools for fairness and accuracy.
Build adaptable course designs that can be refreshed quickly.
